test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 02 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Two pipes can fill a cistern, individually, in 40 minutes and 14 minutes, respectively. There is a pipe located at the bottom of the cistern to empty it. If all the three pipes are opened simultaneously, then the empty cistern gets filled in 20 minutes. How long will the pipe at the bottom of the tank take to empty the completely filled cistern if no other pipe is then open?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Capacity (LCM of 40, 14, 20) = 280 units.

Efficiency: A = 7, B = 20, Combined (A + B − C) = 14.

Efficiency of Outlet Pipe C = (7 + 20) − 14 = 13 units/min.

Time for C to empty = 280 ÷ 13 = 21(7/13) minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 21(7/13) min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time Pipe A = 40 min, Pipe B = 14 min, Combined time with Pipe C (outlet) = 20 min.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Time × Efficiency

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 Pipe A 40 min 280 units 7 
 Pipe B 14 min 20 
 A + B − C 20 min 14 

⇒ Efficiency of **Pipe A** = 280 ÷ 40 = 7

⇒ Efficiency of **Pipe B** = 280 ÷ 14 = 20

⇒ Combined Efficiency (A + B − C) = 280 ÷ 20 = 14

⇒ 7 + 20 − Efficiency of C = 14

⇒ 27 − Efficiency of C = 14

⇒ Efficiency of **Outlet Pipe C** = 27 − 14 = 13 units/min

⇒ Time taken by C to empty = 280 ÷ 13 = 21(7/13) minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 21(7/13) min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Logic

Efficiency of an **inlet pipe** is positive (+), while the efficiency of an **outlet (emptying) pipe** is negative (−).

Net Work Done

If pipe A fills in x hours and pipe B empties in y hours, then net work in 1 hour = (1/x) − (1/y).

Time and Efficiency Relationship

Time is **inversely proportional** to efficiency. If efficiency increases, time taken to complete the work decreases.</p
